title: Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (depression)
description: Nine items on how often depressive symptoms bothered the respondent over the last two weeks, 0–3 each, plus the unscored difficulty question. A screening aid, not a diagnosis: item 9 asks about thoughts of self-harm, so a study using it needs a plan for responding to positive answers.

citation.text: Kroenke K, Spitzer RL, Williams JBW (2001). The PHQ-9: validity of a brief depression severity measure. Journal of General Internal Medicine 16(9):606–613.

source.note: English form as published on phqscreeners.com, read 2026-10-17; the check-mark instruction is left out (the participant picks one option per row).

scoring.text: Sum of items 1–9 (0–27), in phq9_total. Severity bands from the instruction manual: 5, 10, 15 and 20 = mild, moderate, moderately severe and severe. Item 9 (thoughts of self-harm): the manual notes that a positive answer calls for assessing suicide risk, which requires a clinical interview. The difficulty question is not scored.

items.label: Over the last 2 weeks, how often have you been bothered by any of the following problems?

rows.label: Little interest or pleasure in doing things
Trouble falling or staying asleep, or sleeping too much
Feeling tired or having little energy
Feeling bad about yourself — or that you are a failure or have let yourself or your family down
Trouble concentrating on things, such as reading the newspaper or watching television
Moving or speaking so slowly that other people could have noticed? Or the opposite — being so fidgety or restless that you have been moving around a lot more than usual
Thoughts that you would be better off dead or of hurting yourself in some way

items.label: If you checked off any problems, how difficult have these problems made it for you to do your work, take care of things at home, or get along with other people?
